L.561-1 to L.561-50; Décret n° 2017-1094 du 12 juin 2017; Arrêté du 12 juin 2017; Loi n° 2016-1691 (Sapin II); Ordonnance n° 2016-1635; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended; Règlement (UE) 2015/847; Code de commerce, arts. L.123-11-1 et seq.; Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) administered by INPI.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry or competent commercial court

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / non-bankruptcy certificate

Power of attorney for French incorporation agent
Passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority; certified by notary or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of foreign corporate documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator registered with French Court of Appeal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, French Registre national des gels, OFAC SDN List, and PEP databases (World-Check, Dow Jones) at onboarding and periodically. Enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates. Record retention five years. Suspicious transaction reports to TRACFIN; ACPR supervisory oversight.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) / Infogreffe (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language mandatory for all registry filings. Company name may be in a foreign language if written in Latin characters. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated by a sworn translator. The name must be followed by 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the greffier or INPI rejects name clearance, file a reasoned recours before the juge commis à la surveillance du RCS at the competent tribunal de commerce within 15 days of notification (Code de commerce, RCS procedure). For trademark conflict, file opposition before INPI or civil infringement action before the tribunal judiciaire. Parallel administrative appeal to INPI for refusal of certificate de disponibilité. Extension of certificate requires new application before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office accepted only for registered office where a valid domiciliation contract exists and there is a genuine link to company activity. For data center colocation leasing, a virtual office cannot host servers, power, cooling or security infrastructure; the operational data center must be a real facility with appropriate ICPE, fire, labor and environmental compliance. Tax authority may challenge absence of substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for operational data center sites (DREAL, fire safety, labor, tax, ARCEP): 60-80% annual probability of unannounced or routine inspection. Low-to-moderate for administrative registered office if separate: 10-20% annual probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, Livre II, Titre I, Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 (SAS); Articles L. 210-1 et seq. (general provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) via Infogreffe.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) and Déclaration de constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; capital freely set in statuts. Subscription monies must be deposited in an escrow account (compte bloqué) with a bank or notary until RCS registration; funds released upon presentation of Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, sole founding shareholder of [Company Name], a Société par Actions Simplifiée, resolves: (1) to approve the subscription of [Number] shares at [Price] per share, fully paid up; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Address]; (3) to appoint [Name] as Président and [Name] as Directeur Général; (4) to grant full powers to the Président to complete formalities and open bank accounts. This resolution is adopted on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or private deed (no notary required unless contributions in kind)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft statuts in French, specifying corporate name, registered office, object, capital, governance, and share transfer restrictions. Sign by all founding shareholders. If contributions in kind, engage a notary and an appraiser (commissaire aux apports).
required_dossiers: Proof of address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statuts are rejected, amend clauses per RCS feedback and re-sign.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital in Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account with a French bank or notary. Deposit subscription monies. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank refuses, use notary escrow; re-submit with additional KYC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a JAL within 8 days of signing statuts. Include corporate name, form, capital, registered office, and President's name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If JAL rejects, correct notice and republish; retain proof for RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Infogreffe online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation dossier online via Infogreffe: statuts, attestation de dépôt des fonds, proof of publication, President's declaration, and identification documents. Pay filing fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, respond within 15 days with corrected documents; if rejected, re-file after curing defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the Kbis (proof of registration). Register with tax authorities (SIE) for VAT and corporate tax, and with URSSAF for social security. Open a corporate bank account and release escrow funds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis delayed, follow up with greffe; if tax registration delayed, file provisional returns.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) and Préfet de département.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploiter une Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) and Certificat de conformité incendie.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL under the Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE Autorisation with Full EIA Report for installations > 50 MW; Enregistrement for 5-50 MW; Déclaration for < 5 MW.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with arrêté ministériel de prescriptions générales: wastewater pH 5.5-8.5, temperature < 30°C, suspended solids < 100 mg/L; noise limits per ICPE; waste handling per European Waste Catalogue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (SDIS), structural load inspection by accredited bureau (e.g., Bureau Veritas), and workplace safety clearance from Inspection du Travail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities receive automatic SIREN/SIRET assignment upon incorporation; VAT (TVA) registration is required if annual turnover exceeds the threshold, followed by VAT identification number procurement through the impots.gouv.fr portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections available; French corporate entities are subject to mandatory entity-level taxation

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual turnover threshold triggering mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for B2B transactions under Facture Électronique; large enterprises must comply with real-time fiscal clearance via the PEP platform requiring API integration and digital VAT stamping

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods outside the EU and offshore services supplied to non-EU recipients, subject to proof of export and non-repatriation to France
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT with administrative fines up to 80% of evaded tax and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent export declarations

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the French Foreign Exchange Administration for balance-of-payments statistics and external financial relations, with banking prudential supervision and AML/CFT enforcement delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), and exchange-rate policy competence retained at the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro-area monetary policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. As a euro-area member state, France applies the TFEU Article 63 prohibition on restrictions on capital movements between Member States and third countries; no exchange-control permits are required for lease receivables, vendor payments, or equity injections. Current-account transactions (colocation service fees, bare-metal hosting payments, management fees) are completely liberalized under Articles L.151-1 and L.151-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF). Capital-account flows (capital contributions, shareholder loans, guarantees, security deposits) are similarly free but trigger statistical declaration to the Banque de France when the transaction exceeds EUR 15,000. Profit remittance is unrestricted for an SAS subject to standard corporate formalities: approval of distributable reserves by the shareholders, satisfaction of the legal reserve requirement, and, where the recipient is a foreign parent, dividend withholding at 25% unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty (e.g., Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU for EU parents). Payments to French-listed non-cooperative tax jurisdictions (ETNC) under Article 2384 A CGI face a punitive 75% withholding tax and enhanced documentation; the data center colocation model is otherwise free of convertibility hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation deadline, or forced conversion ratio for export proceeds. A French SAS may retain foreign-currency lease income (USD, GBP, CHF) in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts without conversion to EUR. The only compliance obligation is statistical: under the Banque de France balance-of-payments regime (CMF Articles R.151-1 et seq. and EU Regulation (EC) No 184/2005), each cross-border transaction above EUR 15,000 must be reported through the instructing credit institution, which files the external transactions declaration (déclaration de balance des paiements). There is no requirement to liquidate USD or GBP balances within any statutory window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR collections/disbursements) plus Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) for subscribed capital and tenant security deposits
Operational Account (EUR SEPA/SWIFT) with integrated multi-currency sub-accounts for USD/GBP lease flows
Operational Account and cash-pooling structure for automated tenant collections via SEPA Direct Debit
Operational Account with treasury sweep and virtual IBAN segmentation for individual colocation tenant rent collection
Operational Account and documentary trade desk for outbound equipment Letters of Credit (UCP 600)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for domestic euro treasury operations but legally constrained for core banking functions. PSD2-licensed and ACPR-supervised electronic money institutions (EMIs) and EU-passported challenger banks (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Wise Business, Revolut Business) can efficiently execute monthly SEPA ACH debits, virtual IBAN allocation, and FX conversion at transparent rates, and are viable for low-risk operational disbursement accounts. Legal constraints under the E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC and CMF Articles L.525-1 et seq.: EMIs may not grant credit, may not hold client funds as deposits, and must safeguard all e-money funds in segregated accounts at a credit institution or central bank, thereby falling outside the FGDR (French deposit guarantee) scheme. Consequently, an EMI is unsuitable as the sole treasury rail for capital escrow, securitized security deposits, cross-border equity injections, or documentary credit operations. The strategic design therefore mandates a Tier-1 bank as the primary clearing anchor with one or two EMIs as secondary collection acceleration rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: ACPR/AML rules (CMF Articles L.561-5 to L.561-8) require identity verification of the SAS legal representative and each beneficial owner using robust, independent documentation, but do not strictly mandate a physical interview. In practice, Tier-1 French banks require at least one physical onboarding meeting with the SAS président (or a formally mandated France-resident agent holding a notarized power of attorney) whenever the shareholder structure is non-EU or the initial capital injection exceeds EUR 100,000. Remote account opening is permissible where the bank operates an eIDAS-compliant (Regulation (EU) 910/2014) video-identification flow and executes the mandate with a qualified electronic signature; however, most universal banks still condition full treasury activation on presentation of the original Kbis extract, apostilled articles of association, certified passport copies, and a physical or notarially witnessed signature specimen for the authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership: the SAS is held by a foreign holding company and the RBE (Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) declaration has not yet been filed or is incomplete
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed RBE declaration as filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), certified share register with full chain of ownership, group corporate structure chart, articles of association with French notarized translation, tax residency certificates (attestation de résidence fiscale) for each UBO, and sworn declarations of source of wealth for any UBO holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial inbound equity injection exceeding EUR 100,000 from a non-EU jurisdiction into the SAS capital account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extrait du procès-verbal of the extraordinary general meeting approving the capital increase, the capital subscription deed (acte de souscription), the sending bank's SWIFT MT103 trace plus an authenticated letter of provenance from the remitting entity, source-of-wealth statement supported by bank statements and audited financial statements of the parent, passport copies of the contributing shareholders, and a commercial rationale memo describing the colocation leasing business plan and projected customer base.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident président without French fiscal domicile or social security number, creating identity and signature-verification gaps
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract or equally authoritative foreign registry extract not older than three months, notarized passport copy, proof of residential address (utility bill or lease), formal resolution granting the président executive authority, bank mandate forms (pouvoirs bancaires) with certified wet-ink or qualified electronic signature, and a delegation letter appointing a France-resident authorized signatory with operational banking powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media red flags triggered by data center tenant counterparties or third-party treasury service providers located in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU / OFAC / UN sanctions screening results for the full tenant and vendor portfolio, negative-media search reports, executed colocation master service agreements and service schedules, invoice history and rent roll evidencing legitimate commercial relationships, landlord-tenant contractual excerpts with French-law governing clauses, and an internal AML policy confirming transaction monitoring for all cross-border receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual treasury velocity: high-frequency lease settlement sweeps from multiple virtual IBANs to a single central account or to offshore treasury centers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast, colocation rack-lease schedule with rate cards, historical tenant payment histograms, treasury management policy describing liquidity concentration mechanics, explanation of accounting treatment for security deposits vs. operating lease income, and organizational charts of the payment factory showing legitimate cash-pooling rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: route all inbound equity injections via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank) to the SAS EUR account at the designated Tier-1 French bank. The remittance information field (Field 70) must state 'Fonds apport en capital de la SAS' together with a reference to the capital increase resolution. The receiving French bank will map the flow to the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for equity participation under the capital-transactions classification (category 3D), and will automatically file the mandatory declaration for any amount exceeding EUR 15,000. Where the remitting shareholder is treaty-eligible, the bank may request a certificate of tax residence for withholding-treaty application; the SAS treasury must retain the shareholder resolution, updated RCS filing (dépôt modificatif), and proof of registration of the capital increase as verification for the bank's KYC file. SEPA Credit Transfer is acceptable only for EEA-origin euro injections; SWIFT remains the preferred rail for non-EEA funds to preserve the audit trail through Target2 and central bank reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for recurring euro-denominated lease costs and operating expenses: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) via the Target2 ecosystem. Tenant rent collections should be automated through the SEPA Direct Debit (SDD) core scheme, with virtual IBAN segmentation to reconcile individual colocation units. For cross-border vendor payments in USD, GBP, or CHF: SWIFT MT103 with SWIFT gpi for same-day tracking and irrevocable settlement. High-value infrastructure procurements (transformers, uninterruptible power supplies, generators, cooling systems) should be executed through documentary Letters of Credit under ICC UCP 600, with deferred-payment tenors matched to lease receivables, and Incoterms 2020 allocation negotiated at shipment. All disbursements require encoded beneficiary IBAN/BIC validation, automated sanctions screening, and adherence to the Banque de France external-financing reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards (forward exchange contracts) for USD/EUR and GBP/EUR lease income conversion, executed under ISDA documentation with NFC- status exempting the SAS from mandatory EMIR clearing below the clearing threshold.
FX swaps (swap de change) with maturities up to 12 months for temporary cross-currency liquidity matching between USD-denominated vendor payables and USD-denominated colocation receivables.
Cross-currency swaps (long-dated currency swaps) for project-finance debt where the SAS draws foreign-currency loans for data center expansion while servicing euro revenue.
European-style FX options for contingent transaction exposures, such as optional capacity bookings or pending colocation contracts denominated in USD or GBP.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to structurally inconvertible or restricted currencies (e.g., offshore CNY) and subject to ESMA MiFID II product governance; unnecessary for freely convertible EUR/USD/GBP/CHF exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual accounts, including management report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI one-stop filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a court injunction, daily coercive penalties, and liability of the legal representative. France has no automatic statutory strike-off timetable solely for late annual accounts; administrative dissolution or strike-off may arise from separate inactivity, registered-office, or legal-compliance issues.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI one-stop filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation is required solely because a new year begins. An initial filing is required at incorporation, and changes to beneficial-owner information must generally be filed within 30 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial-owner information may lead to court injunctions, fines, and restrictions or removal of the entity from the register in serious or persistent cases. No fixed annual strike-off deadline applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the relevant statutory assessment date: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required for certain controlled-company, group, regulated, or specific transaction circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the French Commercial Code and the Autorité des normes comptables accounting regulations. IFRS is generally relevant to consolidated accounts where applicable and is not the default framework for standalone SAS accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a general annual beneficial-owner confirmation. The SAS must keep beneficial-owner information accurate and file an amendment within 30 days after a change. A share transfer must be recorded in the share-transfer register and shareholder records; a beneficial-owner filing is required if the transfer changes the beneficial-owner information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and shareholders' individual securities accounts
Minute book or secure record of shareholder and corporate-body decisions
Current corporate records identifying the president, directors, and other registered officers
Beneficial-owner information records supporting the filing made with the Commercial Court Registry

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,200 per year for commercial domiciliation or registered-office services, excluding additional mail handling, legal representation, and compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 5,000-15,000 per year for a small or mid-sized SAS requiring a statutory auditor; no statutory audit fee is required if the entity remains outside the mandatory-audit scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for qualifying SMEs on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit; research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) may offset corporate income tax; no data-center-specific tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD (CERFA 12314) together with annexes 2050 through 2059-G; mandatory electronic filing via the EFI portal at impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the e-filing deadline is 15 May of the following year (3 May for paper filers, but e-filing is mandatory for an SAS).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: accounting profit or loss adjusted by schedule 2058-A for non-deductible expenses, tax exclusion, depreciation recapture, and other statutory restatements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source profit attributable to a French permanent establishment or a French commercial operation; do not include foreign-source colocation revenues earned outside the French tax net unless a PE is created in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deficit reportable as carry-forward: quantum of prior-year tax losses deducted from current-year taxable income, supported by schedule 2058-B.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are deductible only if economically connected to the French activity of the SAS; attach a segmented profit/loss account showing the French PE versus other foreign activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: CIR, CII, foreign tax credits, and other imputation systems reducing the corporate income tax charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must satisfy French double-tax-relief rules and any applicable DTA; a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) must support credits from non-French rentals or services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Option for a French tax group (intégration fiscale) where a French parent consolidates SAS results with affiliates sharing one tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The group head must be established in France. A non-resident direct parent cannot itself head the French tax group; the French subsidiary must be the integrating company and a French-resident group head is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related parties: list intercompany colocation leases, rack-space rentals, maintenance fees, and bare-metal server service fees, along with the arm's-length method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete form 2257 if related-party transactions exceed EUR 50,000 or 1% of annual turnover; include the foreign related tenant/parent and the functional and risk analysis for each service charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge on corporate income tax, increasing to 40% if the return is filed more than 30 days after formal notice; monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%; an automatic 5% increase applies to unpaid tax; non-compliance with mandatory e-filing attracts separate fixed penalties; deliberate misdeclaration may trigger 30% or 80% sanctions plus criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for corporate recipients; 30% flat tax for individual recipients; 75% for shareholders resident in non-cooperative jurisdictions; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying EU parent holding at least 5% for two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must submit Form 5000 (individual) or Form 5001 (corporate) to the French paying entity before distribution, have the form endorsed by the home-country tax authority as a TRC, and demonstrate substantive beneficial ownership. If domestic WHT was applied at source, a refund claim must be filed with the local tax office (SIE) no later than 31 December of the second calendar year following the year of withholding. For an SAS, the non-resident shareholder must also evidence that it is the economic owner of the dividends and that no BEPS intermediary was inserted into the payment chain.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: patent, trademark, and similar industrial-property royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 33.33% withholding tax; arm's-length interest paid by a French corporate borrower to a foreign corporate lender is generally exempt under Article 131 quater CGI, otherwise a 30% withholding tax applies (50% for non-cooperative jurisdictions). DTA rates commonly reduce royalties to 0%–5% and interest to 0%, subject to limitation-on-benefits and beneficial-owner conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 in annual turnover or balance-sheet total; groups with consolidated turnover of EUR 750,000,000 or more must additionally file country-by-country reporting.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) register, but the general anti-abuse rule, Article 205 A CGI, and OECD BEPS 12 principles require a French SAS to have real premises, operating employees, and actual decision-making capacity. A colocation SAS must exercise active control over server contracts, power supply, cooling, and client onboarding, and cannot be a mere invoice-passer or subscribing shareholder conduit without triggering recharacterization or denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to invoice colocation or bare-metal hosting services to foreign customers, recording fictitious maintenance fees, or shifting French leasing profits to a low-tax related entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic tax assessment with 40% penalty for deliberate misstatement, increased to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights; monthly late-payment interest at 0.2%; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment for fraude fiscale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or approved the concealment can be prosecuted personally; courts may impose travel bans, freezing orders, restitution of unpaid taxes, and civil liability for the company's tax shortage.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS as a letterbox entity with no employees, no IT engineers, no board activity, and no physical data-center assets while routing rack leasing through the structure solely to obtain treaty relief or reduced WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the abuse-of-rights procedure (LPF Article L64) with an 80% penalty on the re-qualified profit, plus recovery of the underlying tax; criminal prosecution for money laundering of the illicitly shifted profit is also available.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto managers and directors may be jointly and severally liable under LPF Articles L266-L267 for the unpaid tax and penalties; travel bans and imprisonment may apply upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting undocumented third-party cash, cryptocurrency, or payments routed through shell clients for server rack leases; failing to identify beneficial owners of tenant entities or serving sanctioned persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML violations carry administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or twice the value of the proceeds for non-financial professionals; failure to report suspicious transactions to Tracfin triggers further sanctions; EU and French asset-freeze rules may lead to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be sentenced for money laundering (five years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine), face quartering of personal assets, and be prohibited from managing companies; travel bans are commonly imposed in cross-border laundering cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting below-market rack space rentals, bare-metal lease fees, or group service charges to foreign affiliates without benchmarking; withholding required documentation under form 2257 despite exceeding the EUR 400 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Correction of French taxable profit to the arm's-length position; 10% transfer-pricing penalty under Article 1731bis CGI, plus 40% penalty for absence of documentation; double taxation and late-tax interest may also be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing inadequate transfer-pricing documentation can be held civilly liable for the additional tax; if pricing is set with entities in tax-haven countries, joint and several liability for the hidden profits and criminal sanctions may follow.
